unmutated.L1:lock-round-trips: Asserted on Lock.parse and Lock.toJson, static model classes the harness calls directly; a SigilCompiler never reads or writes the lock file, so no compiler implementation can break it. S6:canonical-json already holds the lock's canonical form, and a defect here is a defect in the shared model, not in an implementation of the contract.
unmutated.L1:lock-rejects-reused-code: Asserted on the static Lock.parse reader, which the compiler under test never touches; a broken compiler cannot make the reader accept two selections with one code. The same invariant is enforced by Lock.plus, which every compile path and S3:lines-complete-the-lock go through.
unmutated.L1:lock-rejects-reused-key: Asserted on the static Lock.parse reader, not on a compiler; a compiler implementation has no hook into how a lock file is read. Its twin L1:lock-rejects-reused-code covers the same parse-time rejection path for the code side, and Lock.plus enforces both.
unmutated.L1:lock-rejects-code-zero: Asserted on Lock.parse and Lock.Entry, whose constructor refuses codes below 1; code 0 is the base model's marker in Selection, so a compiler that handed out 0 would already break S1:one-selection-per-tuple. No compiler replaces the lock reader.
unmutated.P1:well-formed-program-accepted: Asserted on the static Program.parse; the compiler under test is not involved, so no broken compiler can make a sound program parse differently. A parser that wrongly refused sound programs would fail every harness program built with Programs.parse before this label is reached.
unmutated.P1:malformed-program-rejected: The 18 malformed texts are fed to the static Program.parse, which is shared model code and not pluggable per implementation. What a compiler adds on top (refusing a program built in code) is the P1:compiler-rechecks-program entry TrustsBuiltProgram.
unmutated.S5:catalog-agrees-with-registry: Asserted on ComponentCatalog.disagreements, a static model method the consumer calls in its own test; it is not one of the SigilCompiler's steps, so a compiler implementation cannot get it wrong. The compile-time half of the projection law is covered by S5:server-private-rejected, S5:unknown-component-rejected and S5:type-mismatch-rejected.
unmutated.S6:declaration-order-independent: Program's constructor sorts inputs by name, guards by input name and context rules by model before any compiler sees them, and case order is the program's meaning, so a compiler cannot observe the order the file was written in. The order the emitter then chooses for its output is held by S6:cases-in-key-order (ReversedCases) and S4:overrides-strictly-ascending.
unmutated.S8:rules-mean-only-and-except: Asserted on the oracle Evaluator.draw, the static model function every S8 check compares an emitted definition against, not on a compiler. A compiler that reads only and except the wrong way round is the InvertedContexts entry, caught by S8:definition-draws-context-rules.
unmutated.T1:tool-reports-missing-lock: SigilTool is the build entry point over text and constructs ReferenceSigil itself, so there is no compiler to substitute; it is model code the Gradle plugin calls. The underlying LOCK_MISSING refusal is mutated through S3:missing-lock-lists-lines (InventedCodes) and S3:lines-complete-the-lock.
unmutated.T1:tool-completes-the-lock: SigilTool.lock is a thin appender over Lock.apply and the compiler's LOCK_MISSING lines, with ReferenceSigil hard-wired, so no implementation of the contract can break it. The lines it appends are held by S3:lines-complete-the-lock (NamespacelessLockLines) and S3:new-selections-append.
unmutated.T1:tool-lock-is-idempotent: SigilTool.lock is static model code over a hard-wired ReferenceSigil, not a pluggable implementation. That a complete lock needs no lines is S3:missing-lock-lists-lines in reverse (a compiler that invented codes would break it, entry InventedCodes).
unmutated.T1:tool-compiles: SigilTool.compile is static model code that parses text and calls ReferenceSigil; the harness cannot swap the compiler inside it. What the compile produces per era is mutated through the S2, S4 and S6 labels, which compile the same programs directly through the compiler under test.
unmutated.T1:tool-is-deterministic: SigilTool.compile calls the hard-wired ReferenceSigil twice and compares the text, so only a defect in the model itself could fail it. Determinism of an implementation's bytes is mutated through S6:repeat-identical (BuildStampedArtefacts) and S6:locale-independent.
unmutated.T1:tool-one-program-per-item: A check inside SigilTool's own loader (two program files for one item are refused before any compiler runs); no SigilCompiler is involved, so no implementation of the contract can break it.
